notes: §1985:X.5.2.3 SR2: "Identifier-1 must be defined as an alphanumeric data item such that its value can be a program-name." CallBinder#BindCall resolves identifier-1 and Identifier1Screen refuses (COBOL1681), through NameTargetRefusal/OperandTargetRefusal, every category but alphanumeric, national and program-pointer; at 85 PIC N and USAGE PROGRAM-POINTER are themselves refused (COBOL0900), so only the alphanumeric arm is reachable. Probes at --std 85: PIC X(8), a 01 group, a group's PIC X(4) child, a subscripted element PTE(2), PN(1:4) and FUNCTION UPPER-CASE("subp") (an alphanumeric function, kb/Work PB5240) all call the program; PIC 9(4) (witness), COMP, PIC A, PIC XXBXX, USAGE INDEX and FUNCTION NUMVAL refused COBOL1681. The messages cite §2023:14.9.4.3 SR1 (wording only).

next.reason: 1985 requires identifier-1 to be 'an alphanumeric data item such that its value can be a program-name'. §2023:14.9.4.3 SR1 allows 'an alphanumeric, national, or program-pointer data item', and §2023:14.9.4.4 GR3 gives each its meaning (alphanumeric or national content 'is the program-name of the program being called'; a program-pointer holds its location). No 1985 rule admits another class (1985 X.5.2.4 GR1 only gives the content's meaning), so 2023 accepts programs 1985 refused; an alphanumeric identifier-1 means the same. Looser, no exception condition introduced for the 1985 case.
